explanations.explanation: That's the answer, baker. Paul doesn't dance around it. He says "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:15). Grace isn't a permission slip, and Paul shuts that idea down in two words.

I get why it tempts people, friend. Grace is so big that somebody was bound to ask if it's a free pass. But Paul answers his own question with "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:15). He doesn't leave a crack in that door.

A little sin here and there sounds reasonable, like a cookie or two off the cooling rack. But Paul doesn't give a single "at times." He says "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:15), and that's the whole answer.

Yes, baker! Paul says "you are slaves to the one you obey" (Romans 6:16). Whoever you keep offering yourself to is the one in charge. It's not about a title on paper. It's about who you're actually listening to.

Good guess, since every adult knows who signs the paycheck. But Paul's picture isn't about a boss. He says you are slaves to "the one you obey" (Romans 6:16). The master is whoever you're actually following.

explanations.answer: The one you were born under
explanations.explanation: That one sounds sensible, friend, like where you start decides where you end up. But Paul points somewhere else. He says you are slaves to "the one you obey" (Romans 6:16), and that's about what you offer yourself to.

Tempting, because everybody wants a No Master option. But Paul doesn't offer one. He says you're a slave either "to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness" (Romans 6:16). Two choices on the table, baker, and no third door.

Right, baker. Paul lays out only two: "slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness" (Romans 6:16). There's no third door marked Nobody's The Boss. I'd love that door too, but it's not in the text.
That's it, baker. Paul says being "slaves to sin" leads "to death" (Romans 6:16). Every master has a destination, and this one's a heavy one.
Sin loves to advertise that one, friend. But Paul says it's "slaves to sin leading to death" (Romans 6:16). The freedom sin promises isn't the freedom it delivers.
Sounds nice, like a warm couch after a long bake. But Paul doesn't say rest. He says "slaves to sin leading to death" (Romans 6:16). That's a very different place to end up.

Yes, baker! Paul says "thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed" (Romans 6:17). Notice he thanks God. The whole moment is a thank-you, not a pat on the back for them.

explanations.answer: Kept every part of the law
explanations.explanation: I see why you'd go there, friend, since law is all over this chapter. But Paul says they "wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed" (Romans 6:17). He's not praising a perfect law record. Just a few verses earlier he says they're "not under law, but under grace" (Romans 6:15).

explanations.answer: Worked to earn their own freedom
explanations.explanation: That would make me tired just reading it, baker. But Paul never says they earned anything. He says they "wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching" (Romans 6:17), and he starts with "thanks be to God." The thanks goes to God.
That's right, baker. Paul says, "You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness" (Romans 6:18). Free from one master, now serving another. And this master is a good one.

Close, but the text says it plainly, friend. Paul writes, "You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness" (Romans 6:18). So it's true. They were set free and then became slaves to righteousness.

explanations.answer: The same parts they once gave to impurity
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Paul says, "Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness" (Romans 6:19). Same parts, new master. I like how practical that is.

explanations.answer: Only the parts never used for sin
explanations.explanation: That would be a short list, friend, and Paul doesn't give it. He says, "Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity… so now offer them in slavery to righteousness" (Romans 6:19). The very parts that once served impurity now get a new master.

explanations.answer: Only the parts the law calls clean
explanations.explanation: Interesting guess, but Paul doesn't sort body parts by the law. He says, "Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity… so now offer them in slavery to righteousness" (Romans 6:19). The same parts, just pointed somewhere new.
That's it, baker. Paul asks about "the things of which you are now ashamed" (Romans 6:21). The word now matters. Looking back, those things don't look so good anymore.
Nope, friend. Paul calls them "the things of which you are now ashamed" (Romans 6:21). Nobody's hanging those on the fridge.
I can see relief fitting, since being free is a big deal. But the word Paul uses is different. He says "the things of which you are now ashamed" (Romans 6:21), so shame is how they look back on them.

I get the thought, baker, but it doesn't match the text. Paul says of the earlier things, "The outcome of those things is death" (Romans 6:21). Then for those set free and slaves to God, "the outcome is eternal life" (Romans 6:22). So the outcome isn't the same.

Right, baker. Before, "the outcome of those things is death" (Romans 6:21). Now, for those set free from sin and slaves to God, "the outcome is eternal life" (Romans 6:22). Death on one side, eternal life on the other. That's a big difference.
Yes, baker! "The gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Romans 6:23). Wages are what you earn, but a gift is handed to you. Paul wants us to see that difference clearly.

I see why you grabbed it, since law shows up around this passage. But Paul's line is "the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Romans 6:23). He's set wages and a gift side by side, and law isn't the one he picks.

That one fits the payday picture, friend. But Paul says wages on one side and gift on the other. The line reads, "the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Romans 6:23). Pay is what you earn, and eternal life is not something you earn.
